- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate and should reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate and should increase forecast, particularly if recent prices are falling.
- Model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings, leading to overshoots in 30-day forecasts — apply smoothing or lagged adjustment for sentiment-driven volatility.
- After a price spike, model frequently continues upward even as sentiment turns negative — correct by introducing a downward bias after the peak.
- Mean reversion is evident when sentiment is neutral or mixed — model should gradually reduce forecast slope toward historical mean of recent 5–7 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence in sentiment-driven momentum — reduce forecast magnitude if sentiment is inconsistent or fading.
